Why MT Matters for Oil & Gas Assets in Kuwait City

Kuwait City hosts KPC's operating companies - KOC, KNPC, KIPIC, PIC and KGOC - coordinating inspection standards across the country. KNPC's Mina Abdulla refinery (approx 454k BPD post-Clean Fuels Project) and Mina Al Ahmadi refinery (approx 346k BPD) anchor the northern industrial belt, while KIPIC's new Al-Zour refinery (615k BPD) is one of the world's largest single-site refineries with integrated LNG import. KOC manages Greater Burgan - the world's second-largest oil field - and its gathering centers, booster stations and water injection networks.

EQUATE (Kuwait/Dow JV) and PIC run ethylene glycol and polyethylene trains. MEW's Az-Zour and Shuaiba power and desalination complexes drive combined-cycle boiler inspection. Every contractor must meet KOC Standards and KNPC Engineering Standards along with API 510/570/653/579 and NACE MR0175.

In Kuwait City, MT earns its place in the integrity stack because of how cleanly it characterises surface and near-surface cracks in ferromagnetic materials, weld toe cracking, casting porosity, fatigue cracks under coating. Productivity on the typical oil and gas workpack here runs 120-180 linear feet of weld per hour, and every recordable indication gets a Level III sign-off. The dominant damage mechanisms we are scoping for on Kuwait City oil and gas assets are creep cavitation in chrome-moly, HTHA on carbon and 1.25 Cr steels, and graphitisation in long-service fired-heater tubes - all of which fall squarely inside the detection envelope of MT when the procedure, calibration block and probe selection are right.

Magnetic Particle Testing Procedure and Technique - Field Detail

Yoke method per ASME V T-754 requires a minimum lifting force of 4.5 kg (10 lb) for AC yokes and 18 kg (40 lb) for DC yokes, verified daily before the first shot. Surface preparation is per SSPC-SP1 (solvent clean) for production work and SSPC-SP3 (power tool cleaning) for in-service inspection through coating up to 0.05 mm. Examination is performed in two perpendicular directions to ensure detection of indications at any orientation, with magnetisation sequence documented on the inspection sheet.

On weld toes the Atlantis approach is wet fluorescent MT (WFMT) with a 7AC blacklight at 3000 microW/cm2 minimum intensity at 38 cm, measured daily with a calibrated radiometer. Bath concentration is verified hourly using a settling-tube test — wet visible bath is 1.2-2.4 mL/100 mL settled volume; wet fluorescent bath is 0.1-0.4 mL/100 mL. For high-temperature inspection above 60 C we switch to dry-powder method per ASTM E709 Section 7.1. Demagnetisation is mandatory after MT on any component that will be welded, machined or operate near magnetic instruments; residual field is verified below 3 gauss using a field-indicator gauss-meter.

Field economics: Productivity on linear weld inspection runs 120-180 ft per hour for a single inspector with WFMT; visible bath increases this to 200-280 ft per hour but at a sensitivity penalty for tight surface-breaking cracks. Consumable cost is roughly $4-8 per linear foot of weld inspected, dominated by the bath itself plus PPE.

Oil & Gas Applications We Cover - Asset by Asset

Atlantis NDT supports the full upstream-to-midstream oil and gas inspection lifecycle: separator vessels under API 510 with a typical 5-10 year on-stream inspection interval; piping circuits under API 570 with TML monitoring on a 5-year interval and CML mapping on 1-3 year cycles depending on corrosion rate; storage tanks under API 653 with a typical 10-year out-of-service inspection plus annual shell integrity walks. Subsea riser inspection is performed by ROV-mounted UT thickness systems for shallow water and by guided-wave and pulsed-eddy-current under-insulation surveys for top-tensioned risers above the splash zone. Crude transmission pipelines are inspected in-line with high-resolution MFL and UT geometry tools, with above-ground anomaly verification using bell-hole excavation and PAUT mapping over the indicated wall-loss area. Asset owners typically integrate the resulting inspection data into a Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) workflow per API 580 / 581, with corrosion-rate trending feeding Fitness-for-Service evaluation per API 579 when wall-thickness or crack-like indications fall outside fixed-equipment integrity limits.

Within Kuwait City's oil and gas base, MT is applied to pressure vessels, separators, storage tanks, transmission piping, subsea risers. The dominant scope shape is turnaround inspection campaigns of 4-6 weeks with 24/7 shift coverage, and our written-practice procedure pack contains the matching MT technique sheets for every one of those asset types.

The oil and gas operators driving the scope volume in Kuwait City and the wider Kuwait market include names such as Saudi Aramco, ADNOC, Shell, ExxonMobil, alongside regional independents and JVs that contract Atlantis on call-out and turnaround agreements.

Local Regulatory Context - Kuwait

Inspection evidence in Kuwait City ultimately satisfies Kuwait Oil Company (KOC), KIPIC and KNPC inspection standards plus the Kuwait Environment Protection Authority. Reports issued by Atlantis NDT carry the dual-stamp combination of ASNT Level III sign-off and the operator-specific procedure reference required for clean audit closure under that regime.

Our Kuwait City crews carry the bilingual procedure binders and digital report packs needed by the regulator, and we maintain pre-qualified mobilisation routes from our regional hubs into Kuwait City so a scope can be executed inside a normal owner permit-to-work cycle rather than running over into the next outage window.
